rules.sentence: Back pain is the leading initial symptom (>85% of cases).
The location of the pain corresponds to the site of infection: the cervical spine in ~10% of cases, the thoracic spine in 30%, and the lumbar spine in 60%.
One exception is involvement at the thoracic level in two-thirds of cases of tuberculous osteomyelitis and at the lumbar level in only one-third.
Neurologic deficits, such as radiculopathy, weakness, or sensory loss, are observed in about one-third of cases of vertebral osteomyelitis.
In brucellar vertebral osteomyelitis, neurologic impairment is less frequent; in tuberculous osteomyelitis, it is about twice as frequent as in cases of other etiologies.

A primary focus should always be sought but is found in only half of cases.
In osteomyelitis caused by viridans streptococci, endocarditis is the source in about half of patients.
Early-onset infection is diagnosed within 30 days after implant placement.
Late-onset infection is diagnosed beyond 30 days after surgery, with low-virulence organisms such as coagulase-negative staphylococci or P. acnes as typical infecting agents.
